headline: Medium-risk shared-workspace and output-chaining issues; no critical compliance gap is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem content and uses uploaded knowledge base files; Semantic Kernel can read/write application-defined files and use MCP/OpenAPI tools. If Dify outputs are fed into SK prompts or plugins, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The shared-state paths make this plausible in default orchestration, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are copied into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin inputs without sanitization
IF either agent ingests shared workspace files as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and instruction/data separation template
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from shared files
Review one representative handoff for prompt-injection markers
Require human approval before executing tool calls from imported text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging across the shared datastore

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write files and both handle secrets or sensitive context: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs, while Semantic Kernel touches application context and plugin credentials. A shared workspace or datastore can expose those data classes across the pair, and both have broad network egress, so leakage is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem or datastore
IF either agent persists prompts, logs, or retrieved files in shared storage
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Turn off shared logging for one test run
Inspect one sample log for secrets or KB excerpts
Restrict network egress to approved model endpoints
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent encryption and access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has server-side shell/subprocess and filesystem write capability; Semantic Kernel has filesystem write and MCP/plugin execution, but no shell. They can still race on the same mutable files or shared memory store, causing overwrite or inconsistent state. The conflict is real if they target the same resources, though not as severe as unrestricted dual-write with git state.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared memory store
IF one agent assumes exclusive ownership of files or records
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Add file-level locks for shared artifacts
Run a quick collision test on one shared file
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an agent/workflow platform that can emit tool-driven outputs, and Semantic Kernel is a kernel-plus-plugins framework that can consume those outputs in downstream function calls. If SK treats Dify text as authoritative, errors can cascade into actions or plugin invocations. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Dify-generated text as direct plugin input
IF no verification step checks Dify outputs before action-taking
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require citations or structured schema from Dify
Log one end-to-end handoff for review
Block direct action execution on unstructured text
requires-engineering: add policy checks before plugin calls

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile states a residency, HIPAA, GDPR, or retention mismatch. The only concrete compliance concern is that Dify touches conversation logs and knowledge base content while Semantic Kernel touches application context and plugin credentials, so a mismatch could arise if the operator routes regulated data through both. The evidence is insufficient for more than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify conversation logs and then forwarded into Semantic Kernel plugins
IF the deployment assigns different retention or residency policies to the two agents
mitigations: Confirm both agents share the same retention policy
Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Check one sample export/delete workflow
Document the data classes allowed in each agent
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
